question: Where can I get the railway network (geometry) of the United States, with line type, electrification, infrastructure manager and traffic?

answer.summary: FRA's North American Rail Network (NARN) Lines, distributed by BTS in NTAD, is the national line layer: 302,774 polylines (235,703 in the US) at 1:24,000 or better, with owner, dispatcher or maintainer marks, trackage rights, passenger-service type and a network class that marks abandoned and out-of-service lines. It has no electrification or traffic field. Reported train counts exist only at highway-rail crossings (FRA Form 71, 438,962 rows). Electrification was found only in OpenStreetMap tags, sampled at two places.
main_caveats: NET separates the active network from abandoned (A, R), out-of-service (X) and trail (T) features. Filter before measuring: US rows total 235,703, of which 81,529 are main network (M).
PASSNGR is the type of passenger service on a line, not a train count or an electrification flag. Do not infer either from it.
RROWNER1-3 mix dispatcher, maintainer and land owner; TRKRGHTS lists railroads with rights, not the operators that actually run trains.
Crossing counts are self-reported: 52% of 438,962 rows give a count year (51,282 rows 2025, 12,274 rows 2019) and 192,201 rows are closed crossings.
Subdivision names and railroad codes differ between datasets (Hartford Line in NARN vs New Haven in the crossing inventory; AMTK vs ATK).
railroads.dot.gov and publications.iowa.gov refused default curl requests (403) and gis.fra.dot.gov did not connect; NARN and crossing data were reachable.
answer.confidence_reason: NARN and the crossing inventory were queried and cross-checked at two corridors (NEC in NJ, Hartford Line in CT); electrification rests on two OSM samples and FRA map pages were unreachable.

attributes.note: NARN polylines, stated 1:24,000 or better: 302,774 features, 235,703 with COUNTRY='US'. Includes yards, sidings, industrial leads and abandoned lines.
NET is the network class (M main, I industrial lead, Y yard, S siding, A or R abandoned, X out of service, T trail); PASSNGR adds passenger service type.
Only OSM tags: contact line, 13 kV, 60 Hz on the New Haven Line; electrified=no on the Hartford Line. NARN and the crossing inventory have no such field.
attributes.gap_note: No official line-level field found in the NARN dictionary or crossing columns. FRA map pages were not reachable (railroads.dot.gov 403, gis.fra.dot.gov no connection). OSM coverage was sampled at two places only.

attributes.note: RROWNER1-3 hold railroad marks for dispatching, maintenance and/or land ownership without saying which role; TRKRGHTS1-9 list railroads with trackage rights.
attributes.gap_note: Roles are merged in one field (3,076 US rows carry a second or third mark) and train operators are not a field. Marks differ between datasets: AMTK in NARN, ATK in the crossing inventory.

attributes.note: Reported trains per day at crossing points (daylight and night through trains, passenger trains per day) with the count year; no per-line tonnage or train total was found.
attributes.gap_note: Crossing counts are self-reported points with mixed years. STB waybill data and state density maps were not opened (Iowa DOT page returned 403 to curl).

sources.summary: FRA's national rail line layer (NARN): geometry, railroad owner marks, trackage rights, passenger service type and network class including abandoned and out-of-service lines.

coverage.geographic: United States, Canada and Mexico: COUNTRY US 235,703 features, CA 64,539, MX 2,532.

unit.value: One row is one line segment between FRA nodes (FRAARCID); MILES and KM give its length. Counts of rows are segments, not routes.
unit.quote: The NARN Rail Lines dataset is a database that provides ownership, trackage rights, type, passenger, STRACNET, and geographic reference for North America's railway system at 1:24,000 or better within the United States.

inclusion_rule.value: All track classes are in one layer: NET separates main network, industrial leads, yards, sidings, abandoned, removed and out-of-service lines, trails and ferries.
inclusion_rule.quote: Indicates which operations is part of the network, spatially

reference_date.value: Revised 2026-10-19 and published 2026-10-20; the layer was created in 2016.

update_frequency.value: Quarterly, per the BTS metadata maintenance frequency.

exclusions.value: Owner, dispatcher and maintainer roles are not separated into fields; the data dictionary has no electrification or traffic field.
exclusions.quote: The same entity may fulfill one or more of these roles on the same line.

key_fields.meaning: Segment identifier and FRA node numbers at its start and end.
Country (US, CA, MX), state abbreviation and FIPS codes.
Reporting marks of railroads in charge of dispatching, maintenance and/or land ownership (FRA Rule 260 codes).
Reporting marks of railroads having trackage rights.
Railroad-defined division, subdivision, branch and yard names.
Passenger service on the line: A Amtrak, B Amtrak and commuter, C commuter, E intercity HSR and commuter, I intercity HSR, R rapid transit, T tourist, D Alaska Railroad.
S on the Strategic Rail Corridor Network, C a connector line.
Number of main line tracks.
Network class: M main, O other track, Y yard, I industrial lead, S siding over 4000 feet, A abandoned, R abandoned and removed, X out of service, T trail, F rail ferry.
Segment length in miles and kilometres.

how_to_use.example_result: First feature: FRAARCID 379940, RROWNER1 AMTK, TRKRGHTS1 CSAO, TRKRGHTS2 CSXT, TRKRGHTS3 NJT, SUBDIV NORTHEAST CORRIDOR, PASSNGR B, TRACKS 4, NET M, MILES 0.93. All 79 matching NJ segments have RROWNER1 AMTK.
steps: Query the FeatureServer layer 0 (maxRecordCount 2000) with where filters such as COUNTRY='US' AND NET='M', or download the whole table as CSV from https://ngda-transportation-geoplatform.hub.arcgis.com/api/download/v1/items/e143f436d4774402aa8cca1e663b1d24/csv?layers=0 (302,774 rows, 43,654,251 bytes).
Filter COUNTRY='US' and choose NET classes: M for the main network, or add I, S and Y if industrial leads, sidings and yards are wanted.
Read RROWNER1-3 as railroad reporting marks (AMTK, UP, BNSF, CSXT, NS...) and decode them with the FRA Rule 260 list cited by the data dictionary at https://doi.org/10.21949/1528950.
Use geometry from the FeatureServer (returnGeometry=true, outSR=4326); the CSV export has no geometry column.
To link traffic, join to the crossing inventory by coordinates (the Wallingford CT crossing fell within 60 m of segment 537093).
reading_traps: COUNTRY covers US, CA and MX; only 235,703 of 302,774 rows are US.
Of 235,703 US rows only 81,529 are main network (M, 132,596 miles); other classes add yards, sidings, abandoned and out-of-service lines.
RROWNER marks can be owner, dispatcher or maintainer; 3,076 US rows have a second or third mark.
TRACKS is 0 on 189,447 rows overall (mostly non-main classes) and on 137 US main-network rows.
SUBDIV and BRANCH are railroad-defined names and do not match the crossing inventory subdivisions.
The hub download links redirect to temporary signed URLs.

problems: The CSV export has attributes only, with no geometry column.
The GeoPackage export is 136,613,888 bytes (header only; not downloaded).

sources.name: Crossing Inventory Data (Form 71) - Current
sources.adds: Reported train counts (through, switching, passenger per day), the year of the count and timetable speed at highway-rail crossings, the only line-adjacent traffic figures found.
sources.summary: FRA Form 71 crossing inventory: railroad-reported through, switching and passenger train counts with count year and timetable speed at 438,962 crossing records.
sources.coverage_note: Points at crossings only; 52% of rows have a count year and 192,201 rows are closed crossings.
sources.data_date: Rows updated 2026-11-23; count years vary (51,282 rows 2025)
caveats: Counts are self-reported and dated per row.
statecode is FIPS; Amtrak is ATK here, AMTK in NARN.

coverage.geographic: United States highway-rail crossings reported by railroads and state DOTs: 438,962 rows, 362,405 with latitude and longitude.

unit.value: One row per crossing record (crossing ID) with trains per day and per week counted at that crossing; closed crossings stay in the table.
unit.quote: It contains the current crossing inventory - one record for each crossing.

inclusion_rule.value: Crossings reported by railroads and state DOTs on Form FRA F 6180.71, public and private, at grade and grade-separated.
inclusion_rule.quote: All such crossings are reported by railroads and state Department of Transportations to the FRA on Form FRA F 6180.71 U.S. DOT Crossing Inventory Form.

reference_date.value: Per row: revisiondate and trainsperyear, the year of the train count. Table rows were updated 2026-11-23 (rowsUpdatedAt).
reference_date.quote: Year of Train Count Data [Box #II.2 on Form 6180.71]

attempts.note: The description points to a data release schedule story that was not opened; rowsUpdatedAt shows 2026-11-23.

exclusions.value: Counts exist only where reported: 228,798 of 438,962 rows give a count year; 192,201 rows are closed crossings.
exclusions.quote: Year of Train Count Data [Box #II.2 on Form 6180.71]

key_fields.meaning: U.S. DOT Grade Crossing Identification Number.
State FIPS code (for example 09 for Connecticut), county code and city.
Primary operating railroad, its subdivision and milepost at the crossing.
Reported train counts at the crossing.
Year of the train count data.
Maximum timetable speed over the crossing.
Crossing coordinates as text, decimal degrees.
Reason for the last update (including Closed) and At Grade, RR Under or RR Over.

how_to_use.example_result: First row: crossingid 500642U, WALLINGFORD, Amtrak, subdivision NEW HAVEN, milepost 0012.65, passenger trains per day 34, daylight through 22, night through 12, switching 2, trainsperyear 2019, max timetable speed 40, lat 41.457314, lon -72.824967, revised 2026-02-17.
steps: Count with $select=count(*); filter by statecode (FIPS text), railroadcode and railroadsubdivision.
Exclude closed crossings with reasondescription != 'Closed' and keep crossingposition = 'At Grade' or all positions as needed.
Read trainsperyear as the year of the count; rows without it carry no dated count.
Match to NARN by coordinates (latitude and longitude are text, cast to numbers) rather than by subdivision name.
reading_traps: statecode is a FIPS code, not the postal abbreviation: statecode='CT' returns nothing.
Amtrak is code ATK here and AMTK in NARN.
typeoftrainservice1 can say Freight while numberpassengertrainperday is 34.
The table has 192,201 closed crossings; 210,164 rows have no count year.
Counts are points on a line, not segment totals, and the count years differ between neighbouring crossings.

problems: Counts are reported by railroads and state agencies; no independent verification was made.
The FRA developer site safetydata.fra.dot.gov (OData) lists the same inventory but has a Sign In link; it was not used.

evidence.claim: Crossings are reported to FRA on Form 71.
evidence.quote: All such crossings are reported by railroads and state Department of Transportations to the FRA on Form FRA F 6180.71 U.S. DOT Crossing Inventory Form.

evidence.claim: The table has train counts per crossing.
evidence.quote: Total Day Thru Trains (6 AM to 6 PM) [Box #II.1.A on Form 6180.71]

sources.name: OpenStreetMap railway ways with electrified, voltage and frequency tags (Overpass API)
sources.adds: The only line-level electrification attributes found: electrified, voltage and frequency on rail ways, sampled on the New Haven Line and the Hartford Line.
sources.summary: Non-official OSM tags are the only electrification data found: contact line, 13 kV and 60 Hz on the New Haven Line sample; electrified=no on the Hartford Line sample.
sources.coverage_note: Two small bounding boxes in Connecticut; coverage elsewhere unknown.
caveats: Volunteer data; a missing tag means unknown.

coverage.geographic: Worldwide; tested only at two small bounding boxes in Connecticut.

unit.value: One way is one OSM rail segment; tag values are text (voltage 13000 is volts, frequency 60 is hertz).

attempts.note: Only data queries were run; no tag documentation page was opened.
Volunteer-edited; no inclusion rule or completeness statement was found.

reference_date.value: Overpass base timestamp 2026-11-24T09:51:14Z on the New Haven query.

key_fields.meaning: contact_line or no on the sampled ways.
Volts and hertz where tagged (13000 and 60 on the New Haven Line sample).
Operator, line name and main or branch usage.

how_to_use.example_result: 5 ways at timestamp 2026-11-24T09:51:14Z: two ways named New Haven Line with electrified=contact_line, frequency=60, voltage=13000, operator Metro-North Railroad; three ways with electrified=no.
steps: Send Overpass QL with a generic client identification; the default curl identification was rejected.
Query way["railway"="rail"] in a bounding box and read the electrified, voltage and frequency tags.
Treat a missing tag as unknown, not as non-electrified.
reading_traps: Hartford Line ways at Wallingford carry electrified=no, while the Metro-North ways near New Haven carry contact_line: tags differ between neighbouring lines.
Tag completeness is not stated; only two small boxes were tested.

problems: The default curl client received 406 Not Acceptable; a generic client identification was accepted.
Several queries returned 502 (server at capacity) and a second public instance returned an empty response once.

operators.note: 863 distinct RROWNER1 marks appear on US NARN rows; the largest are UP (42,446 rows), BNSF (34,967), CSXT (27,990) and NS (27,841).

related_not_answering.name: Census TIGER/Line Rails (MTFCC R1011 Rail Feature, 2024 technical documentation)

open_questions: Is there an official line-level electrification layer? Starting point: FRA's maps page (railroads.dot.gov, 403 to curl) and gis.fra.dot.gov (no connection). Next step: open them with another legitimate client or ask the FRA GIS office named in the BTS metadata.

Is there a segment-level traffic dataset (trains per day or gross tons per mile)? Starting point: STB Carload Waybill Sample documentation and the Iowa DOT railroad traffic density publication (https://publications.iowa.gov/51902, 403 to curl). Next step: open the STB documentation and state DOT GIS portals.
How are RROWNER marks resolved to roles and names? Starting point: the FRA Rule 260 owner codes cited by the NARN data dictionary. Next step: obtain that code list and its role convention.
How complete are OSM electrification tags? Starting point: the two samples in Connecticut. Next step: count rail ways with and without the electrified tag per state when Overpass has capacity.
How do crossing inventory subdivisions map to NARN SUBDIV and BRANCH? Starting point: Wallingford CT (NEW HAVEN vs HARTFORD LINE). Next step: join by coordinates within 60 m and tabulate mismatches.

history.note: First pass: NARN lines and FRA crossing counts tested at two corridors; electrification found only as OSM tags.
